summary: Two boundary defects remain: URL redaction can keep a credential when a query holds an @, and non-finite path reporting has no byte budget. The formatter and serialiser changes are clean.

contract.owns: The described workstreams: logger redaction and serialisation, byte-safe webhook formatting, and non-finite number reporting.
contract.does_not_own: The deferred retry-queue changes and the pre-existing log shipping configuration.

findings.title: Decide URL boundaries from the original string
findings.finding: For `https://host.test?email=a@b.test&token=SECRET` the userinfo pass removes everything up to the `@` in the query, taking the `?` with it, so the query pass finds nothing and `token=SECRET` is logged.
findings.protected_behaviour: Every logged URL loses its userinfo, query and fragment, including a URL with no path.
findings.evidence: logger.ts:26-27 runs two replacements in sequence on an already modified string. Reproduced with the unit harness.
findings.recommendation: Match each URL once and compute its boundaries from the original token. Redact the whole token when an @ appears after the authority.

findings.title: Cap the total bytes of reported paths
findings.finding: The path count is capped at 20, but one path can be as long as the payload. Twenty non-finite values under a very long key produce a report many times the payload size.
findings.protected_behaviour: The report stays within a fixed byte budget whatever the shape of the payload.
findings.evidence: A generated 2 MB payload with one long key and twenty infinite values produced a 40 MB report.
findings.recommendation: Track the bytes of collected paths and stop at the budget, recording the remainder as a count.
